reader.summary: During the week of October 14 to 17, 2026, South Korea faced a cluster of diplomatic, security, and economic pressures. The dominant story was the worsening US-South Korea relationship over an intelligence dispute: Washington halted the prosecution of a former CIA analyst accused of aiding South Korean intelligence, and officials acknowledged that bilateral ties had hit a low point. On the Korean Peninsula, both North and South Korea conducted hypersonic missile tests, with Pyongyang's missile chief publicly questioning Seoul's glide-vehicle trial, underscoring an accelerating arms race. In the economy, the KOSPI index closed at a six-month low as chipmakers slumped amid AI-related worries, and at least one major fund manager shifted allocations away from Korean equities; however, the finance minister insisted the semiconductor outlook remained solid. Separately, South Korea reviewed expanding its military mission in the Middle East, and its relations with Ukraine soured over the handling of North Korean prisoners of war. Domestically, the government turned to coal ahead of a winter gas supply squeeze, and a South Korean official warned that shifting requirements could block the long-planned transfer of wartime command from the US. A minor sports incident involving a South Korean winger at Swansea also drew brief attention.

The KOSPI index closed at a six-month low as semiconductor stocks slumped on AI-related worries, and a $29 billion manager recommended Nigerian equities over Korean ones.
South Korea reviewed expanding its military mission in the Middle East, according to a Reuters report.
Ukraine and South Korea relations soured over the handling of North Korean prisoners of war.
South Korea turned to coal-fired generation as a winter natural-gas supply squeeze loomed.
A South Korean official warned that shifting goalposts in requirements could block the transfer of wartime operational command from the US to Seoul.
South Korea's finance minister told investors the semiconductor market would remain solid at least through next year despite the current slump.
Swansea reported an alleged racial abuse incident toward South Korean winger Ji-sung Eom during a match at Millwall.

display.eli5:
South Korea is dealing with a lot of stress at once right now. The biggest headache is a fight with the United States over an intelligence case where Washington dropped charges against a former spy. At the same time, both Koreas are testing powerful new hypersonic missiles and publicly questioning each other's work, which makes everyone nervous.

The US-South Korea intelligence dispute hurts because sharing secrets is the glue holding the alliance together, and dropping the case feels like Washington is protecting its own people. The missile race is escalating because each side wants to prove its hypersonic weapons are the best, and both are moving fast.

Next week, expect Seoul to demand explanations from Washington and another round of missile-related headlines from the Peninsula. Stock markets will probably stay weak as investors worry about chipmakers and AI investment timelines.

A real surprise would be South Korea suddenly announcing a concrete troop expansion in the Middle East, jumping straight from "we are thinking about it" to "here is the plan." That would shift the story from quiet discussion to visible action.
